title: Phenotyping Mouse Myeloid and Lymphoid Cells by Mass Cytometry
author: Morin, Autier, et al.
materials: Cell suspension preparation is an important step in a mass cytometry protocol, and the tissue dissociation method must be adapted to each tissue to enable complete dissociation while preserving cellular epitopes.5 This step describes how to digest lung and spleen tissues to obtain a high-viability single-cell suspension, as well as how to prepare a single-cell suspension from intraperitoneal lavages.Note: Before harvesting the organs, intravascular lavage is recommended to avoid contamination with blood cells. troubleshooting 2.1.Preparation of lung cell suspension.CRITICAL: Work with freshly isolated lung tissue and not with thawed tissue. troubleshooting 3.a.Dissociate lung samples.i.Place lung sample in petri dish containing RPMI medium supplemented with 10% of FBS on ice.ii.Cut the sample into small pieces using scalpel (2–3 mm).iii.Add 4 mL of digestion solution (as described in the “materials and equipment” section) in gentleMACS C-tubes on ice, and place minced samples in this tube.iv.Insert C-tubes in the gentleMACS dissociator and start the program set to 165 rounds/run for 37 s.v.Incubate tubes at 37°C for 15 min in water bath and shake it every 5 min.vi.Insert C-tubes in the gentleMACS dissociator and start the program set to 2079 rounds/run for 38 s.b.Filter the lysate in 40-μm cell strainer placed on 50 mL Falcon tube and press gently using the plunger of a syringe to complete dissociation.c.Rinse the cell strainer with 5 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS.d.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C.e.Lyse red blood cells.i.Prepare 5 mL of 1× RBC lysis buffer per sample by diluting the 10× RBC lysis buffer (BioLegend) to 1:10 in Milli-Q water.ii.Resuspend cell pellet with 5 mL of 1× RBC lysis buffer.iii.Incubate on a rotary shaker for 5 min at 4°C in the dark.iv.Stop lysis by adding 10 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS.v.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C and discard supernatant.vi.Add 3 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS for a second wash.vii.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C and discard supernatant.Alternative: Lung samples can be dissociated using other enzymatic digestion cocktails, such as dispase, hyaluronidase, or collagenase IV, or through mechanical digestion using other homogenizer.f.Sort dead cells on magnetic column. troubleshooting 4Note: The beads and buffers used to sort dead cells on the magnetic columns are part of the Dead cell removal kit (Miltenyi).Optional: Cells could be count at this step to evaluate the bead volume to add for dead cell sorting (100 μL of beads for up to 10 million of dead cells).Note: 15 ± 5 millions of total cells could be are obtained after entire right lung lobe dissociation with 60 ± 10% cell viability (determined using trypan blue staining).i.Add 100 μL of beads from the Dead cell removal kit and resuspend gently using a pipette.ii.Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.iii.Prepare 3 mL of 1× binding buffer (Dead cell removal kit) per sample by diluting 10× binding buffer to 1:10 in distilled sterile water.iv.Add 400 μL of binding buffer 1× on cell suspension after incubation.v.Insert MS columns on the separator OctoMACS fixed to a magnetic rack and place 15 mL Falcon tubes under the column.Note: The choice of column type depends on the number of cells obtained and cell viability. In this protocol, MS columns are used because less than 10 million dead cells are obtained. If LS columns are chosen, adapt the protocol using the manufacturer’s recommendations of Dead cell removal kit (Miltenyi, Cat#130-090-101: link).vi.Place a 40 μm cell strainer on the top of the column and add 500 μL of 1× binding buffer to humidify cell strainer and column.vii.Add cell suspension on the 40 μm cell strainer placed on the column to filter it and to sort dead cells on the magnetic column.viii.Wash the cell strainer and the column by adding 500 μL of 1× binding buffer and wait until all the buffer has passed through the column.ix.Wash the column 3 more times with 500 μL of 1× binding buffer.x.Recover the 15 mL Falcon tubes containing the live cell suspension.xi.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4°C and discard the supernatant.Note: The cell viability percentage obtained after dead cell sorting is around of 90 ± 5%.2.Preparation of spleen cell suspension.a.Place the tissue in 40 μm cell strainer placed on 50 mL Falcon tube with 1 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS.b.Crush the tissue using the plunger of a syringe.c.Rinse the cell strainer with 4 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS.d.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C.e.Discard the supernatant.f.Lyse red blood cells as described for the lung samples (Step 1, sub-step e).Note: After entire spleen dissociation (healthy mice), 46 ± 18 millions of total cells could be obtained with a mean viability of 80 ± 10%.Note: Spleen tissues can be cryopreserved using a CryoStor CS10 solution (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat#C2874-100ML) according to the recommendations. If the cell viability is lower than 80%, dead cells can be sorted on magnetic column following the protocol above (Step 1, sub-step f).3.Preparation of cells from peritoneal lavage done with 10 mL of 1× PBS supplemented with 2% of FBS.a.Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4°C.b.Discard the supernatant.c.Lyse red blood cells as described for the lung samples (Step 1, sub-step e).Note: In a peritoneal lavage performed with 10 mL of PBS, the mean number of cells recovered is 5 ± 1.5 million for healthy mice and 16 ± 7 million for infected mice.Note: The cells recovered in peritoneal lavages can be cryopreserved in FBS solution containing 10% of DMSO.4.Resuspend cells in RPMI medium and mix an equal volume of the cell suspension with a 0.4% trypan blue solution.5.Count cells on Malassez chamber.

steps.title: Dissociate lung tissue and obtain single cells
steps.instruction: Process freshly harvested lung lobes to generate a viable single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Place lung tissue in a petri dish on ice containing RPMI + 10 % FBS.
Cut tissue into 2–3 mm pieces with a scalpel.
Add 4 mL digestion solution (see Materials) to a gentleMACS C‑tube on ice and transfer minced pieces.
Run gentleMACS program 165 rounds/run for 37 s.
Incubate tubes at 37 °C for 15 min in a water bath, shaking gently every 5 min.
Run gentleMACS program 2079 rounds/run for 38 s.
Filter lysate through a 40‑µm cell strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube; press gently with a syringe plunger to aid dissociation.
Rinse the strainer with 5 mL 1× PBS + 2 % FBS.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Prepare 5 mL 1× RBC lysis buffer (dilute 10× BioLegend buffer 1:10 in Milli‑Q water).
Resuspend pellet in 5 mL 1× RBC lysis buffer; incubate on a rotary shaker for 5 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Stop lysis by adding 10 mL 1× PBS + 2 % FBS; centrifuge 400 × g 10 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Wash once with 3 mL 1× PBS + 2 % FBS; centrifuge 400 × g 10 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Optional dead‑cell removal:
Add 100 µL Dead‑cell Removal beads (Miltenyi) per up to 10 × 10⁶ dead cells; resuspend gently.
Incubate 15 min at room temperature.
Prepare 3 mL 1× binding buffer (dilute 10× binding buffer 1:10 in sterile water).
Add 400 µL binding buffer to the cell suspension.
Place MS column (Miltenyi) in OctoMACS magnetic rack; position a 15 mL Falcon tube beneath.
Place a 40‑µm cell strainer on the column; add 500 µL binding buffer to humidify.
Add cell suspension onto the strainer/column to filter and retain dead cells.
Wash column three times with 500 µL binding buffer each; collect flow‑through (live cells) in the Falcon tube.
Centrifuge collected live cells at 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare spleen cell suspension
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from mouse spleen.

substeps.instruction: Place spleen on a 40‑µm cell strainer positioned over a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 1 mL 1× PBS + 2 % FBS.
Gently crush tissue with a syringe plunger.
Rinse strainer with 4 mL 1× PBS + 2 % FBS.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Lyse red blood cells using the same RBC‑lysis procedure described for lung cells (Step 1 sub‑step e).

steps.title: Prepare peritoneal lavage cells
steps.instruction: Process intraperitoneal lavage fluid to obtain a cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge lavage (10 mL PBS + 2 % FBS) at 400 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant.
Lyse red blood cells using the same RBC‑lysis procedure described for lung cells (Step 1 sub‑step e).

steps.title: Resuspend cells in RPMI and add trypan blue
steps.instruction: Resuspend the harvested cells in RPMI medium and mix 1 : 1 with 0.4 % trypan blue solution.

steps.title: Count cells on Malassez chamber
steps.instruction: Determine cell concentration using a Malassez counting chamber.

steps.title: Prepare antibody cocktails on ice
steps.instruction: Make separate 50 µL surface‑antibody and intracellular‑antibody cocktails in Eppendorf tubes on ice using the titrated antibody dilutions.

steps.title: Aliquot 3 × 10⁶ cells
steps.instruction: Transfer enough cell suspension from step 5 to obtain 3 × 10⁶ cells.

steps.title: Adjust volume with Maxpar PBS + 2 % FBS
steps.instruction: Add Maxpar PBS supplemented with 2 % FBS to bring the volume to 1.5 mL.

steps.title: First wash of cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Second wash of cells
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL Maxpar PBS + 2 % FBS, centrifuge 400 × g 5 min 4 °C, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Cisplatin live/dead staining
steps.instruction: Stain cells with 0.5 µM Cisplatin to discriminate live and dead cells.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 5 mM Cisplatin stock 1:1000 in Maxpar PBS to obtain 5 µM intermediate.
Further dilute 5 µM solution 1:10 in Maxpar PBS to make 0.5 µM (250 µL per sample).
Add 250 µL 0.5 µM Cisplatin to the cell pellet; resuspend.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Quench by adding 5 × the volume of Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer.
Centrifuge 400 × g 5 min 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend in 1 mL Maxpar PBS; centrifuge again 400 × g 5 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Incubate cells with FcBlock to prevent non‑specific antibody binding.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 100 µL FcBlock solution per sample by mixing 6 µL 0.5 mg/mL FcBlock stock with 94 µL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer (1 µg FcBlock per 10⁶ cells).
Add 100 µL FcBlock solution to cells; resuspend with a P100 pipette.
Incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Wash by adding 1 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer; centrifuge 400 × g 5 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Surface antibody staining
steps.instruction: Label surface antigens with the prepared antibody cocktail.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cell pellet in 40 µL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer (final volume 50 µL).
Add 50 µL surface‑antibody cocktail; mix gently.
Spin 5 s in a microcentrifuge.
Incubate 30 min at room temperature (after 15 min, gently resuspend).
Wash with 3 mL Maxpar Cell Staining Buffer; centrifuge 400 × g 5 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Fix and permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells and prepare them for intracellular staining using the Foxp3/Transcription Factor Staining Buffer Set.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 3 mL diluted FixPerm solution (1:4 FixPerm concentrate in kit Diluent) per sample.
Add 3 mL diluted FixPerm to cells; resuspend gently.
Incubate 30 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge 900 × g 10 min 4 °C; discard supernatant (pellet becomes transparent and slippery).
Prepare 6.5 mL 1× permeabilization buffer (dilute 10× buffer 1:10 in Milli‑Q water).
Wash cells with 2 mL 1× permeabilization buffer; centrifuge 900 × g 10 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Add 40 µL 1× permeabilization buffer to the pellet; incubate 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Intracellular antibody staining
steps.instruction: Stain intracellular targets with the prepared antibody cocktail.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL intracellular‑antibody cocktail; resuspend gently.
Incubate 30 min at room temperature (after 15 min, gently resuspend).
Add 2 mL 1× permeabilization buffer; centrifuge 900 × g 10 min 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Repeat the wash (add 2 mL permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 900 × g 10 min 4 °C, discard supernatant) for a second time.
After the second wash, remove all residual volume carefully.

steps.title: Formaldehyde fixation
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 2.5 % formaldehyde before DNA intercalation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL 2.5 % formaldehyde by diluting 16 % stock 1:6.4 in Maxpar PBS.
Add 1 mL 2.5 % formaldehyde to the cell pellet; resuspend gently.
Incubate 10 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge 900 × g 10 min 4 °C; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Iridium DNA intercalation staining
steps.instruction: Stain nuclei with iridium intercalator for mass‑cytometry detection.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL 0.125 µM iridium solution by diluting 125 µM stock 1:1000 in Maxpar Fix and Perm buffer.
Add 1 mL iridium solution to the cell pellet; resuspend gently.
Incubate 1 h at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C; up to 48 h at 4 °C is permissible).
